bodyPart.en: Teeth (as given in later tables; the Ashtadasha Stotram itself names no body part)

bhairava.en: Not named in the Ashtadasha tradition

history.en: Alampur stands on the Tungabhadra near its confluence with the Krishna. The Jogulamba temple is in the same complex as the Navabrahma temples, nine Shiva temples built by the Badami Chalukyas in the 7th and 8th centuries. The original temple was destroyed by the Bahmani Sultans in 1390; it was rebuilt on its former site in 2005, and the original image was installed in the new temple.

story.en: According to the Puranas, Sati, the daughter of Daksha, gave up her life in the fire of her father's sacrifice after he insulted her husband Shiva. Grieving, Shiva carried her body across the world until Vishnu's discus divided it, and each place where a part fell became a Shakti Peetha. Tradition holds that Sati's teeth fell here. Adi Shankara's Ashtadasha Shakti Peetha Stotram praises the goddess here as 'Alampure Jogulamba'.

en: The goddess is shown seated on a corpse, with a scorpion, a frog and a lizard on her head.
The temple shares its complex with the Navabrahma temples of the Badami Chalukyas.
Alampur lies near the confluence of the Tungabhadra and the Krishna.

timings.en: No official timings are published; check locally before visiting.
